_comment: Per-example pixel budgets for pixel.spec.mjs. Three maps, and an example
must appear in exactly one of them or in none.
budgets — the most differing pixels this example may have and still pass.
An example in none of these maps gates at zero. A budget is set from a
measured maximum, never guessed, and is capped at 0.5% of the image.
A budget more than ten times its observed difference FAILS: a slack
budget is a stale budget, and the fix is to lower the number rather than
to leave a blanket over the example.
pending — not yet gated. Still runs, still prints its observed difference,
and is reported as pending rather than as passing. This is how the check
lands without a 66-way red build: the first run is a census, not a
skips — will not be compared, each with the reason. A skipped example is
still executed, and if it would now pass at zero the run FAILS with
'remove the skip'. A skip that outlives its reason is the tolerance

skips.audio-player.default: The `asChild` divergence `parity-divergence.json` records slot by slot: upstream draws a `<button>` around each media-chrome element and the reader draws one element, so every control is a different box. media-chrome also paints its own icons from a web component the page has to upgrade, and until it does the two sides draw different glyphs.
skips.chart.default: Only one side can draw. `ChartContainer` puts the caller's children inside recharts' <ResponsiveContainer>, which sizes an inner wrapper to 0x0 for anything that is not a recharts element — so the reference renders the chrome and no plot, whatever the example passes it. A reference that drew a recharts <LineChart> instead would be a second design rather than a port, which parity/README.md forbids, and it was also the only example whose pixel count moved between runs. The chrome is still compared: parity.spec.mjs measures every data-slot box and 37 computed properties on both sides. This example passed at zero for as long as neither side drew: chart_style/2 returned "" and the <style> emitted its own source text.
skips.controls.default: Only one side draws it: React Flow's component renders null outside a mounted graph, and `parity-divergence.json` records the whole of that. A box compared against nothing is not a tolerance to measure.
skips.conversation.default: `<StickToBottom.Content>` is two elements upstream — an outer box it scrolls, carrying `scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges`, and an inner one holding the content — and the scroller recipe folds a component into one function because its parts have to agree about one scroll position. So the gutter is on a different element here, and the platform's scrollbar sits in a different place. Every slot still gates at zero in `parity.spec.mjs`.
skips.edge.default: React Flow ships a stylesheet, `canvas.tsx` imports it, and the parity application therefore loads it: its `.react-flow__edge-path` colours the line, and the class sits beside the `stroke-1 stroke-ring` AI Elements writes. The storybook does not ship the library — which library an application loads is the application's decision, the way the markdown renderer is — so the two lines are the same curve in two colours. `parity.spec.mjs` still compares the element and its 37 computed properties.
skips.mic-selector.default: The same `asChild` as `plan.default`, plus a list only one side can draw: upstream reads the microphones from `navigator.mediaDevices`, which reports nothing without a permission prompt, and a server has no such list at all. `parity-divergence.json` records the four slots this shows up on; the trigger differs by too much of its own box to compare what is painted.
skips.open-in-chat.default: The `asChild` divergence `parity-divergence.json` records: upstream draws a menu item around each link and the reader draws the link, so the two lists are sixteen pixels apart in height and every row sits at a different y.
skips.panel.default: Only one side draws it: React Flow's component renders null outside a mounted graph, and `parity-divergence.json` records the whole of that. A box compared against nothing is not a tolerance to measure.
skips.plan.default: Upstream draws two elements where the reader reads one, twice over: AI Elements writes `asChild` and this shadcn build is Base UI, whose equivalent is `render`, so `<Collapsible asChild><Card>` and `<CollapsibleTrigger asChild><Button>` each nest instead of merging — and the second of those is a <button> inside a <button>, which axe reports and is right to. Taking `asChild` at its word is a decision against upstream's own page, and `parity-divergence.json` records the same one slot by slot. Every other AI Elements example gates at zero.
skips.prompt-input.default: The submit button is at the other end of the footer, because the class list is not merged at render: `parity-divergence.json` has the whole of it. A button 366 pixels from where the other side draws it is not a tolerance to measure.
skips.shimmer.default: Both sides animate, and a screenshot of an animation is a race. Upstream moves `background-position` with `motion` and `LiveBase.Shimmer` moves it with the same Web Animations API, from the same two keyframes — but neither run starts on the same frame, so what is compared is two phases of one gradient. `parity.spec.mjs` still measures the box and its 37 computed properties on both sides.
skips.toolbar.default: Only one side draws it: React Flow's component renders null outside a mounted graph, and `parity-divergence.json` records the whole of that. A box compared against nothing is not a tolerance to measure.

reasons.scroll-area.default: 91 px, stable across three runs, scattered over twelve lines of wrapped text rather than clustered. Markup is byte-identical, positions match to two decimals, and font smoothing, text-rendering and body classes are the same on both sides — this is glyph rasterisation, not a component difference. Budget is the measured maximum times 1.5, per PLAN.md.
